title: Class Up Treatment
text: According to Father, among the three slaves, Rabbit Man was leveling up the fastest, I say. While the mixed-breed Lizardman was sitting at Lv 25, Rabbit Man was climbing at a pace that had already reached Lv 33. Racial differences and various other factors were probably at play, or so I judged. Incidentally, Father had gone out slaying monsters together with Kuro-chan and the other Filolial-samas, raising his own level substantially and completing every enhancement method available, so he was now in a state where not even Ceremonial Magic could put him down.

However… despite leveling up quickly, Rabbit Man’s stat growth was poor. Magical aptitude in all attributes, huh… yes, that reminded me of Riska. Though surely Rabbit Man’s stats were growing better than Riska’s? That one barely grew at all until Lv 80. So growing at all put it in a slightly better category, I suppose. If leveling up was this fast, boosting stats through aptitude enhancement should be no trouble at all, indeed.
“……Level isn’t everything.”
“Yeah, I know. Right now I’m just trying to learn some magic too.”
“Make sure you come back to combat training properly.”

Rabbit Man nodded with some complicated emotion swirling behind the gesture. Hmm? Was that it? Perhaps when Rabbit Man had been standing in for Big Sister, there’d been no one else to compare against, so he’d just been swinging a dagger up close. But this time, with the mixed-breed Lizardman and the Wolf around, maybe he was trying to learn magic with his role in mind. Perhaps it was similar to how, depending on the loop, Big Sister sometimes focused mainly on magic instead of using a sword.
“Don’t get all moody about it. I’m not going to fall behind Shion forever either, you know.”
Rabbit Man raised his arm with a wry smile, as if trying to live up to the mixed-breed Lizardman’s expectations, but the arm suddenly spasmed and fur sprouted along it in a flash.
“Ow… ow ow ow… ahaha. Guess I still can’t quite pull it off.”

Rabbit Man laughed awkwardly, troubled by the way his joint had bent unnaturally. Every so often, like some kind of seizure, parts of his body would just transform on their own. The mixed-breed Lizardman watched this partial beastification quietly.
“Beastification, huh… must be rough, not being able to control it.”
“Yeah, but the symptoms have been getting a lot better lately. Iwatani-sama’s been giving me massages every day.”

Look, Rabbit Man said, showing off the arm now that the spasm had passed and it had returned to normal. It hadn’t broken; it was back to its original shape. Come to think of it, he’d seemed unable to use one hand before, but now both hands worked fine.

“I just wish we could find something more fundamental—either a real cure or at least a dramatic reduction in symptoms. If we could manage that, I think Teo could move more freely, and it might even affect his stat growth.”
Father murmured this thoughtfully.
“This is already more than enough. If anything, I think I’m in a blessed situation.”
Rabbit Man answered. The mixed-breed Lizardman sighed in what looked like agreement.
“Hero-sama, what’s wrong?”
The Siltvelt envoy chose this moment to step into the tent and ask Father, who was in the middle of a break.
“Ah, I was just wondering—does Siltvelt have any treatment for Teo’s condition? It’d be great if there was some way to cure it.”
“If I recall, it was hereditary beastification insufficiency, correct?”
“Yeah.”
“Well… Siltvelt tends to operate on survival-of-the-fittest principles, so there’s a general lack of consideration for those born with inherent disadvantages.”
“So there hasn’t really been research into it?”

“No, that’s not quite it either. Even if something is lacking, there’s always the possibility it’s compensated for elsewhere, so I can’t say there’s nothing at all. It’s just that, overall, there’s a heavy emphasis on raw strength, and clever strategists are rather rare…”
“Elephant’s foster father was apparently a general renowned for his strategic mind, I say. If I recall… Janon, I believe it was.”
I tend to forget things easily, but when it came to Elephant—who got along so well with Kou and the Filolial-samas—I remembered perfectly well.

“Janon, was it… Yes, indeed, a strategist who made a name for himself in past battles. So Elmelo was a knight trained under that man… No wonder he seemed unusually cultured for someone from Fuhanto. That explains it.”
Quite right. Elephant’s birth family was a clan of foolish muscle-heads, after all. Small fry that Elephant could crush without even trying, if she got serious.
“I’m no expert either, so I can’t say for certain, but there are those who require a high level before they can beastify. We also know of cases where Class Up unlocks certain aptitudes.”

If I recalled correctly, Tiger Guy had once mentioned that leveling up allowed him to beastify. And Class Up unlocking aptitude… ah, I remembered! Big Sister had become a Raph-species beastman by doing a Class Up as a Raph-species. I felt like Big Sister was somewhere quietly furious at me for recalling unnecessary things, but surely that was just my imagination. She had a not-entirely-displeased look on her face as Father petted her. Filo-tan came charging over toward Father and Big Sister, trying to wedge herself into the mix. I wanted in too, indeed. Yes-pyon, indeed!
“Class Up—that’s the method you can start using from Lv 40 onward, right? So you’re saying if he levels up a lot or does a Class Up, he might gain control over it?”
“I can’t say that with certainty. After all… Class Up is something only granted to those recognized by the state, so it’s not something that can be handed out casually.”
The Siltvelt envoy said this with the nuance that performing a Class Up purely for the sake of treatment was, frankly, a bit questionable.
“In Melromarc it costs money and requires permission, if I remember right.”
“Father surely won’t get permission approved, will he?”
“Ah… yeah. Probably not.”
Given the state of the kingdom, no permission would come through until the Queen returned.
“How lamentable, in the middle of all this damage from the Waves.”
The mixed-breed Lizardman spat out bitterly.
“Exactly! With a disaster like the Waves upon us, I can’t possibly see any justice in squabbling like this. Why can’t people realize this is the kind of outrageous behavior villains pull in stories?”
Truly, exactly right. I agreed wholeheartedly with Rabbit Man’s words.
“……Even if you do a Class Up, it’s not like beastification is guaranteed to follow. If it were that simple, no one would struggle.”
The mixed-breed Lizardman continued.
“Has Shion ever gone through a Class Up?”

At Father’s question, the mixed-breed Lizardman looked away. It was the face of someone who didn’t want the topic pressed further. There was also the matter of Lv Reset. Could it be that the mixed-breed Lizardman had experienced an Lv Reset as well? Did that mean he’d wanted to beastify but hadn’t been able to? But wait… in a previous loop, hadn’t the mixed-breed Lizardman been beastified? Did that mean he couldn’t manage it now? Hmm… well, having done it once meant he could do it, but there was no obligation for me to say so. If Father consulted me about it, I’d answer then.
“……So, in terms of treatment for Teo’s condition, the approach would be leveling up and Class Up, then?”
“It’s not quite that simple, unfortunately. There’s a chance it could actually worsen the beastification insufficiency.”
“Is that so?”
“Yes. Beastification causes that much of a transformation, and there are documented cases of people losing themselves entirely, dominated by instinct.”
Saying this, the Siltvelt envoy glanced at the Wolf. Ah, right, I recalled the Wolf was indeed dominated by beastly instinct.
“Wauu.”
Rather fierce in temperament, that one. One could say it only behaved thanks to Father having tamed it.
“There are also many cases where part of the body remains permanently fixed in a beastified state, so caution is necessary.”
“……Right. So Teo’s basically carrying around a bomb—we need to be careful.”

Rabbit Man clenched his fist quietly, looking frustrated. He seemed to be feeling some impatience too. The mixed-breed Lizardman silently placed a hand on his shoulder, as if to say not to worry too much about it. A commendable attitude, I say. Keep striving, the both of you, so as to be of use to Father.
